mission_09: Remarkable! You have demonstrated the Central Limit Theorem using an exponential population (highly non-normal). The sample means are approximately Normal with mean ≈ 1 (the population mean) and standard error ≈ 1/sqrt(30). The KS test confirms normality of the sample means. As sample size increases from 5 to 100, the KS statistic decreases, showing better Normal approximation. The CLT is why the Normal distribution is so fundamental — it emerges naturally from averaging. This theorem justifies statistical inference methods and explains why many ML algorithms that assume Normality work well even when the underlying data is not Normal.
